text: The claim is refuted — 0-dimensional biomaterials such as nanoparticles and quantum dots (e.g., black phosphorus or cerium oxide nanodots) can actively induce osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and immunomodulation, so they do possess inductive properties; however, the retrieved evidence (NOS superoxide/peroxynitrite injury and mGluR6 ON-bipolar-cell transmission) is entirely off-topic and provides no support for either position.
